## What this measures, and what it does not

This is a **quantization-scheme simulation at the attention-output boundary**
and nothing below it. It predicts what the concurrently-ported per-tensor FP8
D256 kernel's long-context quality *should* look like if it is implemented
correctly.

Explicitly **not** claimed, in the spirit of `upstream/CLAIMS.md`:

* **Not a model-quality statement.** No downstream task outputs, logprobs or
  task accuracy are simulated. The saturation lesson cuts both ways: a metric
  that moves here has not thereby been shown to move anything downstream.
* **Not a measurement of either kernel.** No CUDA kernel and no cuDNN engine
  executes. Only `quant.py` -- the normative preprocessing implementation --
  is production code here; every scheme's *attention* is plain fp32 PyTorch,
  which is what makes them comparable.
* **Not cuDNN.** Schemes 3/4 model the per-tensor FP8 descale contract (one
  scalar per operand). Per claim **K11**, cuDNN's FP8 SDPA does not accept
  D256 at all, so no direct comparison is possible or implied.
* **Not real activations, and the absolute levels do not transfer.** These are
  synthetic distributions. See "Why the lab column reads ~3% and not ~1%".

**Geometry** mirrors production: T=128 query rows as the *tail* of an N-token
context (prefix = N-T, bottom-right causal), Hq=24, Hkv=4, D=256,
sm_scale=1/16. Data is generated in fp32 (the reference) and rounded to bf16
(what the operator consumes), so the bf16 row is the common floor under every
quantized scheme. Every scheme is evaluated by dequantize-then-fp32-attention;
`lab+P (5b)` additionally applies the kernel's normative E4M3 P rounding at
448*r_t, using the **online running-tile-max** form -- verified against
`oracle_a.attention` at max row-rel L2 = 2.03e-03
(the floor is oracle_a's own bf16 output cast).

**Read the pairs, not the columns.** `per-tensor (3)` vs `lab (5)` compares
operand quantization alone. `+P row (4)` vs `lab+P (5b)` compares the two
complete FP8 attention pipelines. Mixing across the P boundary flatters
whichever side is missing its P rounding.

## 6. Mechanism: the per-tensor descale is set by the global extreme

Per-tensor amax over the whole K / V tensor, by depth. A per-tensor scale is a
max over N x Hkv x D samples, so it *grows with N* whenever the tail is heavy;
a per-64-tile scale is a max over 64 x 256 samples and does not.

| dist | N=4,096 | N=32,768 | N=131,072 | N=262,144 | N=446,335 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| gaussian K/V | 5.719 / 5.344 | 5.812 / 5.5 | 5.812 / 5.594 | 5.812 / 5.938 | 5.812 / 5.938 |
| heavy_t3 K/V | 109 / 100.5 | 210 / 168 | 288 / 556 | 332 / 1120 | 1072 / 1120 |
| rope_like K/V | 27 / 5.656 | 27.12 / 5.656 | 27.12 / 6.094 | 27.38 / 6.094 | 27.38 / 6.094 |

## 7. Why the lab column reads ~3% and not ~1%: per-operand ablation

One operand quantized through `quant.py` at a time, everything else bf16-exact.
`p_only` is E4M3 P at 448 with exact operands.

| term | gaussian N=4,096 | gaussian N=446,335 | v_massive N=4,096 | v_massive N=446,335 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Q only (INT8 per row + rotation) | 0.75% | 0.75% | 0.0049% | 0.00046% |
| K only (INT8 per 64-tile + centre + rotation) | 0.98% | 0.98% | 0.0055% | 0.00052% |
| Q and K together | 1.20% | 1.21% | 0.0063% | 0.00059% |
| V only (E4M3 per 64-tile + centre) | 2.67% | 3.14% | 0.012% | 0.0013% |
| P only (E4M3 at 448) | 2.52% | 2.66% | 0.08% | 0.07% |
| mean ‖O‖ per row (the denominator) | 0.4165 | 0.0395 | 100.0 | 100.0 |
| ‖V channel mean‖ | 0.2542 | 0.0241 | 100.0 | 100.0 |
| fraction of V tiles on the vs_max/16 floor | 0.000 | 0.000 | 0.000 | 0.000 |

The QK half of the lab scheme lands at **1.20%** -- the ~1% class
the repo's history records. The V and P halves are each ~2.5-3%, and they are
large *because the denominator is small*: with zero-mean iid V, the attention
output is an average of ~N_eff random vectors, so `mean ||O||` is
0.416 at N=4k and 0.0395 at
N=446k, and E4M3's ~2.5% RMS element-wise relative error lands directly on that
small number. Real activations carry large channel means (the massive-activation
case), which put a floor under ||O||; the `v_massive` column is that regime, and
the identical scheme reads 0.0013% there. Neither number is the real
one -- what transfers is the *comparison*, which is why every table is also
reported as a ratio.

## 8. Honest interpretation

1. **Per-tensor FP8 is flat in depth on well-conditioned data and collapses in
   the tail with depth on heavy-tailed data.** On `gaussian` and `rope_like` the
   per-tensor mean error does not move from 4k to 446k (4.61% -> 4.65%,
   14.60% -> 14.96%), because the per-tensor amax barely moves
   (K 5.72 -> 5.81, 27.0 -> 27.4). On `heavy_t3` the per-tensor K amax grows
   109 -> 1072 and the V amax 100 -> 1120 over the same span, and the damage
   lands in the **tail, not the mean**: worst-row cosine collapses
   0.894 -> 0.501 -> 0.302 -> 0.270 -> **0.049** and worst-row relative error
   climbs 58% -> 96% -> 113% -> 126% -> **136%** (error exceeding signal), while
   the mean over the same cells is non-monotone and ends *lower* than its peak
   (11.1% -> 14.8% -> 13.7% -> 12.8% -> 12.1%). Even the
   plan's mandated worst-**head** aggregate misses it (12.9 -> 16.9 -> 16.0 ->
   15.9 -> 15.4%, non-monotone): at 128 rows per head, averaging 128 rows is
   already enough to hide it. The depth signal of a per-tensor scale is a
   worst-**row** phenomenon.
2. **The lab scheme's advantage is the transforms, not tile granularity.**
   `tile-nocentre (3b)` is per-row-Q / per-64-tile-K/V E4M3 with centering and
   rotation removed. On `gaussian` it is indistinguishable from per-tensor
   (4.63% vs 4.65%) and on `rope_like` it is effectively identical
   (14.91% vs 14.96%): E4M3 is a *floating* format, so a coarser amax costs
   almost nothing until the subnormal floor is reached. Granularity earns its
   keep only on `heavy_t3` (12.08% -> 7.80%, 1.5x). The rest of the gap to
   `lab (5)` -- `rope_like` 14.91% -> 3.52% (**4.2x**) and `v_massive`
   0.51% -> 0.001% -- is bought by K/V mean-centering plus the rotation.
   Reporting this result as "per-tensor vs per-tile scaling" would be an
   unearned conclusion; it is "with vs without the SageAttention-family
   transforms", which is the scope claim **K9** already narrows.
3. **The P-scale policy is not where per-tensor loses.** `+P tensor (4b)` (one
   per-tensor amax on the normalized P) and `+P row (4)` (the online-softmax
   scale 448, which is what a flash-style kernel -- cuDNN's included -- actually
   does) agree to within **1.4% relative in every one of the 25 cells**. Taken in
   quadrature, P rounding contributes the *same* error term to both pipelines:
   2.63% (per-tensor) vs 2.66% (lab) at gaussian/446k, 2.65% vs 2.69% at
   rope_like/446k. Claim **K3**'s "448 is the exact per-row FP8 amax for P" is
   confirmed as costing nothing relative to any per-tensor alternative -- and P
   rounding is emphatically not a free operation for *either* scheme, which is
   why schemes 3 and 5 must not be compared against 4 and 5b.
4. **The lab scheme drifts mildly with depth; the mechanism is a systematic norm
   shrink and is only partly identified.** `lab` goes 2.92% -> 3.35% (gaussian)
   and 3.01% -> 3.52% (`rope_like`) from 4k to 446k, tracked by `norm_ratio`
   0.99968 -> 0.99364. Two candidate mechanisms are *excluded by measurement*:
   the vs_max/16 P-underflow floor never engages (fraction of V tiles on the
   floor is 0.000 at every depth, r_t_min 0.67 -> 0.58), and the V-mean dilution
   ratio ||vmean||/||O|| is depth-invariant at 0.61. What remains is an E4M3
   rounding bias in the centred V whose fixed part grows in relative terms as
   ||O|| shrinks 10x with depth. It stays well inside the plan's [0.98, 1.02]
   `norm_ratio` hard gate and vanishes entirely when V has a channel mean
   (`v_massive`: norm_ratio 1.00000 at every depth). Recorded as an observation
   with a partially identified mechanism, not as a claim.
5. **The bf16 yardstick reproduces the recorded implementation-swap band, which
   is what licenses the rest of the table.** `bf16 (2)` (input rounding only) is
   0.29-0.35% and `bf16-arith (2b)` (plus bf16 P and bf16 output) is 0.41-0.47%
   on `gaussian` and `v_outlier` -- the repo's recorded 0.31-0.45%
   attention-output control band, reproduced without tuning. On the structured
   distributions the yardstick itself moves (0.71-0.98%), which is exactly why
   every number is also given as a ratio to its own cell's control.

## 9. What the ported per-tensor FP8 D256 kernel should therefore show

Falsifiable predictions for the port's numerics gate. All are attention-output
(boundary (a)) statements on *this* synthetic geometry; a real-capture run will
move every absolute level and must be re-anchored to its own bf16 control.

* **Ratio to the lab scheme, essentially flat in depth.** Comparing operands
  only (3/5): **1.4-1.6x** on benign data (`gaussian`, `v_outlier`), **4.2-4.9x**
  on RoPE-structured keys, **3.7-4.6x** heavy-tailed. Comparing the complete
  pipelines (4/5b): **1.25-1.34x**, **3.4-3.7x**, **2.9-3.6x**. Use whichever
  pairing matches whether the port quantizes P; do not mix them.
* **If the port reads ~3% rather than ~15% on `rope_like`, it is not running a
  per-tensor descale** -- something in the pipeline is centering K, and the
  comparison is invalid.
* **The gate must read worst-ROW, not just worst-head.** On `heavy_t3` the
  per-tensor mean and worst-head aggregate are both non-monotone in depth while
  the worst row degrades monotonically to cosine 0.049. A worst-head-only gate
  will report "no depth regression" through a row that has lost its direction
  entirely.
* **`norm_ratio` is the cheap tell for absent centering.** Per-tensor carries a
  systematic, depth-persistent **+0.65%** output-norm inflation on
  massive-activation V and **+0.78%** on RoPE-structured K; the lab scheme sits
  at 1.00000 and 0.993-1.000. This never leaves the plan's [0.98, 1.02] hard
  gate, so it must be *reported as a diagnostic*, not relied on as a gate.
* **P quantization is not a differentiator** (a ~2.6% error term in quadrature
  for both schemes). A port showing a large P-attributable gap has a P-scale
  bug, not a scheme difference.
* **Nothing here licenses a statement about downstream task outputs, logprobs or
  task accuracy.** The input-logprob delta is saturated and cannot rank
  backends.

## 10. Reproduce

```bash
# needs the CUDA torch environment; the plain env has no torch and skips
# tests/kernel for the same reason. `python3 -m pytest -q` is unaffected --
# testpaths is `tests`, and this probe adds no tests.
python3 probes/quality/pertensor_vs_finegrained.py --check-oracle --ablate
python3 probes/quality/make_results.py          # regenerates this file
```

Deterministic: one base seed per distribution (recorded in the JSON), Q drawn
once per distribution independent of N, K/V drawn in fixed
32,768-row blocks with per-block seeds so a shallow cell's
context is a bit-exact prefix of a deep one's. Whole sweep:
15.9 s, 6.21 GiB peak
on one RTX 4090.
